elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires the Company to pay a Termination Payment and expressly characterizes it as a “liquidated amount.”

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not separately impose or authorize any penalty payable by the Company.

elements.element: The fee is payable only upon early termination by Customer.
elements.evidence: The trigger is any event in which the Company “terminates this Agreement”; it is not limited to termination before the end of the agreed term or otherwise defined as early termination.

elements.element: The early-termination fee does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is the lesser of the existing formula and three months' fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer due to early termination.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that the Termination Payment is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company by reason of termination of the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline retains a Customer-payable liquidated termination amount, so it fails the preferred position. Although it adds the required three-month cap and sole-liquidated-amount protection, it does not confine the payment trigger to early termination; it applies whenever the Company terminates the Agreement. Accordingly, the fallback is incomplete. The changes otherwise preserve the existing payment structure and do not alter unrelated commercial terms.
